claims.text: Density Functional Theory calculations can be used to tune the magnetic behavior of non-equiatomic high-entropy alloys.
Density Functional Theory calculations can be used to tune the magnetocaloric behavior of non-equiatomic high-entropy alloys.
Density Functional Theory can predict the total energies of different alloy configurations.
Density Functional Theory can predict the magnetic moments of different alloy configurations.
Predicted total energies and magnetic moments can guide tuning of magnetic and magnetocaloric properties.
Density Functional Theory has limitations in predicting complex magnetic behavior.
The accuracy of Density Functional Theory predictions for non-equiatomic high-entropy alloys is uncertain.
Density Functional Theory predictions can be tested by comparison with experimental measurements of magnetic moments and magnetocaloric behavior.
A mismatch between Density Functional Theory predictions and experimental measurements would falsify the hypothesis.
